BUG in rounds.js line 101: I tried to assign to an optional chaining expression `player.state.weapon?.state?.mag = ...`. That's a JavaScript syntax error — you can't assign to `?.` expressions.

Canvas still missing! The body has 3 children (#game + 2 script tags) but no canvas inside #game. The HUD also didn't build.

Diagnosis: In hud.js, the createHud function calls `rootEl.innerHTML = ...` on document.body. This REPLACES the entire body content — including the #game div that the renderer just appended the canvas to, and the script tags!

```js
// BUGGY hud.js
export function createHud(rootEl) {
  rootEl.innerHTML = `<div id="hud">...`;  // <-- replaces body content!
```

The order in main.js is:
1. `document.getElementById('game').appendChild(renderer.domElement);` — canvas added
2. `const hud = createHud(document.body);` — body.innerHTML replaced, canvas destroyed
Fix HUD bugnya

```
$ agent-browser open "http://localhost:8080/index.html?shot=start&seed=1"
$ agent-browser eval "(() => { const c = document.querySelector('#game canvas'); const ctx = c.getContext('webgl2'); const pixels = new Uint8Array(c.width*c.height*4); ctx.readPixels(0,0,c.width,c.height,ctx.RGBA,ctx.UNSIGNED_BYTE,pixels); let s=0; for(let i=0;i<pixels.length;i+=800) s+=pixels[i]+pixels[i+1]+pixels[i+2]; return Math.round(s/(pixels.length/800*3)); })()"
10  // brightness avg = 10/255 — almost black
```

WebGL IS supported (renderer info: ANGLE SwiftShader). Three.js itself works (tested with a minimal cube scene — got bright orange).

The issue is my scene's dark materials + dark fog + low lighting. The lab map's floor color was #0d1219, walls #12161e, fog #050810. Even with lights, MeshStandardMaterial responds PBR-style and stays dark.

I need to brighten:
1. The palette colors (lighter base)
2. The material colors in world.js
3. Increase light intensity
4. Increase tone mapping exposure
5. Push fog far distance so it doesn't darken the scene
